t: Sort Linked List Already Sorted Using Absolute Values - One-Pass Pointer Surgery
o: The list is sorted by |val| ascending and must be relinked to sort by val. The absolute ordering forces negatives to appear with growing magnitude - e.g. [0,2,-5,5,10,-10] - so negatives arrive in decreasing order (each later one is smaller) while positives already arrive ascending. Exploiting that structure allows an O(n) relink: prepend every newly met negative node to the front. With up to 10^5 nodes, the follow-up asking for O(n) is clearly the intended destination.
k: Positive values already appear in ascending order; negatives appear in decreasing order because their magnitudes grow along the list.
Prepending each newly encountered negative node to the head stacks them into ascending position automatically.
The task reduces to one pass of constant-time pointer surgery with no copying and no allocation.

a.i: Harvest all values into an array, sort it, and write the values back through the existing nodes. It ignores the special precondition entirely but is simple and hard to get wrong.
s: Traverse once collecting node values into an array.
Traverse again writing the sorted values back into the nodes.
a.t: O(n log n) - sorting the value array dominates.

a.n: Approach 2: One-Pass Head Insertion of Negatives
a.i: Since magnitudes grow along the list, negatives show up in decreasing value order; moving each to the front of the list stacks them so the earliest-seen negative ends up deepest - producing an ascending negative block ahead of the untouched ascending positive block. Keep a dummy before head, prev (starting at the dummy) and cur (starting at head): detach cur behind prev, relink it right after the dummy, and resume from the detached node's successor.
s: Anchor a dummy node before head; set prev = dummy and cur = head.
If cur.val >= 0, advance prev and cur one node.
Otherwise unlink cur (prev.next = cur.next), push it to the front (cur.next = dummy.next; dummy.next = cur), then continue from prev.next.
Stop when cur falls off the end and return dummy.next.
a.t: O(n) - every node is examined once with constant-time relinking.
a.sp: O(1) - a dummy plus two pointers.

w: Articulate the invariant before touching pointers: negatives arrive most-shallow-first, so front insertion reverses them into ascending order while positives stay put. Trace [-1,-2,3] (the abs-sorted input can start negative) and single-node lists during practice - both expose off-by-one relinking mistakes instantly. If the precondition were dropped, the answer becomes list merge sort in O(n log n) time and O(1) space; mentioning that pivot shows command of linked-list fundamentals.
